1. Introduction to Jurassic English™ Level 3
1.1
Mission
Statement:
The
Literacy
Pivot
and
Abstract
Reasoning
At Level 3: Expansion, the Jurassic English™ curriculum undergoes its most signiﬁcant cognitive shift.
Designed for learners aged 10–12, Level 3 is engineered to navigate the "Literacy Pivot"—the critical juncture
where language instruction transitions from describing the immediate, concrete world to reasoning about
abstract, universal ideas (e.g., justice, memory, collective responsibility, ecological survival). The mission is to
cultivate Divergent
Thinking: the capacity to hold, analyze, and justify two equally defensible interpretations of
a single text.
1.2
Pedagogical
Positioning:
The
B1
Threshold
Level 3 is the bridge across the A2 →  B1 threshold. It marks the departure from highly scaﬀolded, teacher-led
reasoning (Level 2) into Independent
CEIW
Construction and Student-Led
Socratic
Discourse. At this level,
students do not just answer questions; they interrogate the text, their peers, and the author's underlying
assumptions.
1.3
Standards
Alignment:
CEFR
A2
 → 
B1
&
CCSS
Anchors
The Expansion level is mapped against rigorous international benchmarks, ensuring that intellectual
development translates directly to measurable academic proﬁciency.

1.4
Core
Cognitive
Progression:
The
Divergence
Engine
Level 3 advances the "Stratigraphy of Cognition" through a four-step framework demanding high-level
synthesis:
1. Subtextual
Observation: Moving beyond explicit narrative to locate implied meaning, subtext, and
unstated motives.
2. Divergent
Evaluation: Mapping "Fault Lines"—identifying the exact moment in a text where two opposing
moral interpretations become equally valid.

3. Independent
Justiﬁcation: Constructing a formal argument (Claim →  Evidence →  Warrant →  Impact)
without sentence-stem scaﬀolding.
4. Systemic
Reﬂection: Formally connecting human narrative choices to larger ecological and systemic
consequences.
1.5
World
Wise
Learning
—
Publisher
Statement
World Wise Learning (WWL) categorizes the A2-B1 transition as the highest-attrition phase in language
acquisition (the "B1 Plateau"). Level 3 prevents stagnation by raising the intellectual stakes. By treating English
as a medium for solving profound ethical dilemmas rather than a subject to be memorized, we force the
necessary linguistic adaptation. This manual provides the operational architecture to guide students through
this rigorous intellectual terrain.

Level: Ages 10–12 (CEFR A2 →  B1)
Subject: English Language Arts (Jurassic English™ Level 3: Expansion)
Duration: 45 minutes
Overall
Learning
Goals
Students will open the Bridge
to
Terabithia dig site by separating Katherine Paterson's explicit text from the
dense subtext beneath it. The novel works almost entirely through implication — what Jess feels is rarely
named, but always traceable through what he does. Today: train the eye for B1-level subtextual observation.
Teacher
Pre-Note:
This
text
moves
toward
a
death
by
drowning.
Today's
lesson
opens
before
that
event.
Frame
the
text
honestly
—
students
should
know,
in
general
terms,
that
loss
is
part
of
the
story.
The
Cool
Down
Pass
and
Regulation
Station
are
essential
throughout
this
cycle.
Co-teach
with
a
counselor
available
if
possible.
The
manual
is
clear:
"Do
not
rescue
them
from
the
friction."
That
includes
grief
friction
—
but
it
does
NOT
mean
ignoring
it.
It
means
scaﬀolding
it,
holding
the
standard,
and
trusting
students
to
do
the
work.
Speciﬁc
Learning
Objectives
1. Students will independently regulate and locate the Cool Down Pass.
2. Students will distinguish explicit text from inferential subtext in the opening chapters.
3. Students will locate, dual-code (yellow=explicit, blue=inferred), and cite at least three pieces of evidence —
at least one of which requires inference to understand.
4. Students will articulate the diﬀerence between "what the text states" and "what the author implies" using B1
markers.
